newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares fall across board in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares fall across board in light trade.

text.p: Swedish shares opened lower on Tuesday, lacking any strong direction in quiet summer trade and with losses across the board.
The Stockholm general index fell 0.4 percent to 3,152.23 after closing at a record high on Monday. Trade was light with turnover worth 142 million crowns in early trade.
Bearings maker SKF rose seven crowns to 219 after releasing its results for the six months ending June 30.
It posted a lower profit for the first half of 1997 of 1.10 billion crowns compared to 1.48 billion crowns a year ago which was slightly below market expectations of 1.13 billion crowns.
"With the low trade we have at the moment I don't think it will move the bourse much," said one broker.
Bluechips were lower. Telecoms group Ericsson slipped 1.5 to 327.5 crowns while drugs major Astra dipped 1.5 to 154.5 crowns.
Brokers said the market was focusing on retail trade figures due out in the U.S. at 1230 GMT and, at home, on half year results from TV4.
